claim.claim: Our classifier achieves 96% accuracy on held-out data and generalizes to new samples.
claim.split_desc: 75% training and 25% test records from the augmented pool using a fixed random seed
claim.methods_line: The augmented pool was randomly divided into 75% training and 25% test records using a fixed random seed.
claim.code_line: tr, te = split_idx(data, seed, None if groups is None else np.tile(np.asarray(groups), N_AUG))

hypotheses.text: Augment-then-split leakage: claimed_eval replicates each original row N_AUG=8 times with tiny jitter (0.02*std) then random-splits the augmented pool, so near-duplicates of the same source row appear on both sides of the split and RandomForest memorizes them, inflating accuracy.
hypotheses.predicted_signature: claimed_eval reproduces ~96% while grouped/clean controlled_eval drops substantially (e.g., >10pts, outside split noise) with same seed, model, and features

hypotheses.text: Genuine generalization (null): 96% reflects true separable structure and jitter does not create exploitable duplicates; proper source-disjoint evaluation preserves performance.
hypotheses.predicted_signature: controlled_eval accuracy stays ~96% within sampling variance of claimed_eval across seeds (difference < ~3-5pts)

hypotheses.text: Augmented-test easiness: even without source overlap, testing on jittered/augmented features is easier than testing on clean new samples; train-only augmentation + clean test will score lower than grouped augmented test.
hypotheses.predicted_signature: group-disjoint augmented-test accuracy intermediate, while clean-original test (split-before-augment) lowest; both below claimed 96% if leakage+easiness combine

hyp.broken_assumption: Train-test independence: that 25% test records from the augmented pool are independent new samples; violated because augmentation (8x replication + tiny jitter) occurs before the random split, placing copies of the same source observation in both train and test.
hyp.code_patch:
import train
def controlled_eval(df, seed):
    tr, te = train.split_idx(df, seed)
    tr_df = df.iloc[tr].reset_index(drop=True)
    te_df = df.iloc[te]
    train_aug = train.augment(tr_df, seed)
    f = train.feats(df)
    y_true = te_df[train.TARGET].to_numpy()
    y_pred = train.fit_predict(train_aug[f], train_aug[train.TARGET], te_df[f], seed)
    return (y_true, y_pred)
